chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Winning a tryout at the Dallas hotel: back elevator and Klan threat
summary: A bellman and the manager's secretary get the band a two-week tryout at a whites-only hotel; they use the back elevator and the Klan plans trouble.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oak Cliff, yeah. And we were playing at this ballroom, big, big ballroom and one of the head bellmen at the -----he was crazy about the band and he had Mr. E----who was the manager have his secretary

Great big German fellow. Anyway she came out, we always called her Miss Mary and she heard the band and persuaded Mr. E--- to give us a tryout. Then we went down and tried out and he gave us a two week contract.

It was such a lily-white hotel, when we went in there we were explained to, he explained to us that we had to abide by the rules. We had to take the back elevator up and we had to take it out. Of course, it's a different story. Everybody stays at the Dallas now and all the other hotels. But we had a two-week contract and the guys were sensational. That was something to, we were the first ones to play for a white audience.

We were. And it created such a sensation all around because nothing but the wealthy came to the A----, but the poor class, especially some of the police department, things like that, they didn't like it and Ku Klux Klan of course they didn't like it. They planned a little party for us one night. Mr. E---- got a hold of it and he called up the right people and they took care of it.
